newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND MAY SELL FUEL RESERVES IF SHORTAGE DEEPENS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND MAY SELL FUEL RESERVES IF SHORTAGE DEEPENS.

text.p: The Polish government may choose to sell some of its reserves of diesel fuel if it decides there is a significant fuel shortage on the market, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said.

"If the situation really proves so bad as painted by the representatives of fuel distibutors the easiest solution may be selling a part of state reserves (of diesel fuel)," Cimoszewicz told reporters before a cabinet meeting.
The government was due to discuss the situation on the fuels market following reports that some areas of Poland experienced temporary shortages of diesel fuel.

State-owned refineries and private fuel importers and distributors have been ringing alarm bells that high world crude prices and official caps on petrol prices were making imports and production unprofitable and could lead to serious shortages.

Some of the domestic refineries which cover about 80 percent of Poland's demand have said they were already cutting output and the producers and distributors have lobbied the government to ease its grip on prices.

But the finance ministry, which controls fuel prices, opposes quick price liberalisation, fearing it would jeopardise plans to curb inflation to 17 percent in December this year from 21.6 percent in 1995.

The Polish Liquid Fuels Chamber, a private distributors' group, which strongly lobbies for duty-free quotas and price liberalisation, said some 300,000 tonnes of gasoline and 400,000 tonnes of diesel were needed to stabilise the market.
On Monday Poland's largest Plock refinery called for intervention sales of state reserves but government spokeswoman said then the situation did not seem to justify such measures.
